newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: TIMELINES - Today in History - May 16.
newsitem.headline: TIMELINES - Today in History - May 16.

text.p: ** BIRTHDAYS **
The man considered the greatest of all French writers, HONORE DE BALZAC, was born in 1799.
Australian jurist SIR JAMES BLAIR, who was also a pioneer motorist (driving more than 4,000 kilometres through Queensland in 1908 and rarely using roads), was born in 1870.
American actor HENRY FONDA was born in 1909. He was awarded a posthumous Oscar (best actor) for "On Golden Pond" (1981), and was the father of JANE and PETER. He died on the 12th of August 1982.
American bandleader and clarinettist WOODY HERMAN was born in 1913.
Pianist, entertainer and sequin-freak WLADZIU VALENTINO LIBERACE was born in 1919. He died on the 4th of February 1987 of a brain tumor (unofficially of Aids).
American actress DEBRA WINGER was born in 1955.
Soviet gymnast OLGA KORBUT, who stole the show at the Munich Olympics in 1972 with two gold medals and one silver, was born in 1955.

American pop singer JANET JACKSON was born in 1966. She is the youngest of the nine JACKSON clan children. She first appeared with her brothers in 1973 and in then in "Fame". In 1986 she had success with hits such as "What Have You Done For Me Lately" (1986), "When I Think Of You" (1986), "Let's Wait Awhile" (1987), "Miss You Much" (1989) and "Rhythm Nation" (1989).
Argentinian tennis star GABRIELLA SABATINI was born in 1970.
** EVENTS **
1703 : French writer of fairytales CHARLES PERRAULT,
whose collection "Conte De Ma Mere L'Oye" was translated into English as "Tales Of Mother Goose", died.
1763 : SAMUEL JOHNSON, British writer and lexicographer,
met his future biographer and travelling companion JAMES BOSWELL for the first time in TOM DAVIE's bookshop in London.
1888 : A scheme for constructing a giant bridge across

the English Channel was described in a Paris Journal. It would have been high enough to allow all vessels to pass beneath it, and was estimated to cost around 64 million dollars to build (a lot of money back then, but look at the cost blow-out of the Channel tunnel).
1888 : EMILE BERLINER gave the first demonstration of a
flat recording disc to members of the Franklin Institute in Philadelphia.
1929 : The first Academy Awards (Oscars) were presented

by the American Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences. The awards were given out by Academy President DOUGLAS FAIRBANKS, and the winners included JANET GAYNOR, EMIL JANNINGS and director LEWIS MILESTONE. CHARLIE CHAPLIN was a runner-up, while AL JOLSON received nothing. The nickname "Oscars" appeared in 1931.
1943 : In World War Two, British Lancaster aircraft
succeeded in bombing the Mohne and the Eder dams in Germany's industrial Ruhr basin using a bouncing bomb.
1969 : The Who guitarist PETE TOWNSEND spent a night in a
New York jail for kicking a policeman off stage.
1980 : DOCTOR GEORGE NICKOPOULOUS was indicted in Memphis
on 14 counts of over-prescribing drugs to 11 patients, including ELVIS PRESLEY and JERRY LEE LEWIS.
1983 : DIANA ROSS reunited with MARY WILSON and CINDY
BIRDSONG to appear as the "Supremes" for the 25th birthday celebrations of Motown Records.
1984 : Popular American author IRWIN SHAW died.
1989 : The first successful hole-in-the-heart operation
performed on an adult was carried out on 66 year-old EILEEN MOLYNEAUX at the Brook Hospital in London.
1990 : American entertainer SAMMY DAVIS JUNIOR died of
throat cancer. He was an international celebrity, appearing on Broadway, in films and on television, and published two 'memoirs', "Yes I Can" in 1965 and "Why Me ?" in 1989.
1990 : A Japanese businessman paid 82.5 million dollars

for the VAN GOGH painting "Portrait Of Dr Gachet". Paper manufacturer RYOEI SAITO was the highest bidder for the work, that went under auction at Christie's in New York. It was one of VAN GOGH's last paintings before he shot himself in 1890.
1991 : France's first woman Prime Minister EDITH CRESSON
took office after being appointed by President FRANCOIS MITTERAND.
1991 : Queen ELIZABETH, on a tour of the United States,
became the first monarch to address Congress.
1996 : ROMANO PRODI, leader of the victorious Olive Tree
alliance in the Italian elections, was asked to form the new government.
